STEP 1 - Scene: A salad-style lunch plate: roasted potato wedges, bulgur/couscous salad with roasted peppers and red onion, a dollop of creamy white sauce (yogurt-type), and a mixed green leaf salad with cucumber and red onion slices, topped with a little grated yellow garnish.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 530 cm² (treating it as a dinner plate). Food covers most of the right and center, roughly 80% of the plate.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Roasted potato wedges (herbed, oil-glazed)
- Bulgur/couscous salad with pepper, red onion, cucumber
- Mixed leaf salad (red and green leaves)
- Creamy white sauce/dressing dollop
- Cucumber slices and red onion rings
- Small amount of oil on potatoes

STEP 4 - Area (% of vessel, total ≈ 80%):
- Potato wedges: 25% = 133 cm²
- Bulgur salad: 15% = 80 cm²
- Mixed leaves: 25% = 133 cm²
- Creamy sauce: 5% = 27 cm²
- Cucumber/onion/other: 10% = 53 cm²

STEP 5 - Volume (area x height):
- Potatoes: 133 cm² x 2.5 cm = 333 ml
- Bulgur salad: 80 cm² x 1.5 cm = 120 ml
- Leaves: 133 cm² x 3 cm = 400 ml
- Sauce: 27 cm² x 0.5 cm = 14 ml
- Cucumber/onion: 53 cm² x 1 cm = 53 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Potatoes (dense cooked pieces, ~0.7): 233 g
- Bulgur salad (grain, ~0.8): 96 g
- Leaves (0.15): 60 g
- Sauce (1.0): 14 g
- Cucumber/onion (0.6): 32 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Potatoes, roasted with oil: ~150 kcal/100 g → 350 kcal
- Bulgur salad with veg: ~120 kcal/100 g → 115 kcal
- Mixed leaves: ~20 kcal/100 g → 12 kcal
- Creamy sauce: ~100 kcal/100 g → 14 kcal
- Cucumber/onion: ~20 kcal/100 g → 6 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 435 g and ≈ 497 kcal. This is plausible for a full-looking side-and-salad lunch on a dinner plate, with the potatoes contributing most of the energy.
